newsitem.title: UK: London cabs scrap float, to opt for equity partner.
newsitem.headline: London cabs scrap float, to opt for equity partner.

text.p: London taxi operator Computer Cab Plc said on Wednesday that it had cancelled its plans to float its shares on the London Stock Exchange and instead was set to choose an equity partner.
The group which operates 2,100 taxis was due to float its shares on the Alternative Investment Market through a placing at 80 pence a share with dealings scheduled for April 4.

Computer Cab -- which runs cabs with computerised ordering and payment systems -- informed the LSE about the decision in a brief notice on Wednesday but a source close to its plans said its decision was influenced by a group of drivers who were opposed to the listing.
A weak market also influenced its move, the source said.
The initial market capitalisation would have been around 8.25 million stg.

The issue would have raised 3.3 million stg after expenses, mainly for reducing borrowings, increasing working capital and funding the installation and marketing of the company's Mobistar automatic vehicle location and taxi despatch system.
"The company would look at various proposals...for a partnership," the source told Reuters.
Computer Cab is believed to have received proposals from a few publicly-quoted firms, both local and foreign, mostly from the technology sector.
Computer Cab is wholly owned by the Licensed Taxi Drivers' Association. LTDA had no intentions to dilute its ownership below 51 percent.
